title: USB audio over USB/IP
hypothesis: A USB Audio Class 1 speaker served by GpuVM's own USB/IP server inside the VM and attached with usbip-win2 (Microsoft-signed drivers) is driven by Windows' inbox usbaudio.sys like real hardware, so WASAPI loopback captures it and Sunshine carries the VM's sound to Moonlight without Steam, VB-CABLE or test signing.

results.notes: 2726 URBs, 5,166,720 bytes of isochronous audio received, 1 expected stall (MS OS string descriptor 0xEE)

conclusion: Adopted as the way to give the VM audio. usbip-win2 0.9.8.0 installs silently with only its client; both drivers are signed by Microsoft Windows Hardware Compatibility Publisher and no root certificate is added; attach works without restarting. Windows names the output 'Altavoces (GpuVM Audio)' and drives it with usbaudio.sys. Loopback reads the real signal and Moonlight receives it at a level equal to or above Steam Streaming Speakers. Still to do before shipping: run the server as a service that survives restarts and re-attaches, a pid.codes PID of our own, latency and glitch measurements over a long session.
